query: For the equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni alloy and its equiatomic quaternary and ternary subsets that are single-phase FCC after thermomechanical processing, what testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain why their mechanical properties differ during deformation and failure when constituent count alone is inadequate? Specify a controlled comparison, predictions relative to the quinary baseline, the applicable boundary conditions, supporting evidence, and a result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Lattice distortion, resulting from differences in atomic radii, affects dislocation mobility and interaction with solute atoms, leading to variations in mechanical properties among the equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni alloy and its equiatomic quaternary and ternary subsets.
generation.intervention: Investigation of the role of lattice distortion on mechanical properties, including additional experimental techniques such as in-situ TEM deformation experiments to validate the role of lattice distortion
generation.structural_mediator: Lattice distortion (e.g., due to differences in atomic radii)
generation.mechanism: Lattice distortion affects dislocation mobility and interaction with solute atoms, leading to variations in mechanical properties
generation.predicted_outcome: The quinary alloy will exhibit improved mechanical properties compared to its quaternary and ternary subsets due to reduced lattice distortion, while the ternary subsets will show increased lattice distortion and decreased mechanical properties
generation.uncertainty: The main risk is that lattice distortion may not be the primary cause of differences in mechanical properties, and additional experimental techniques are needed to validate its role

falsification_experiment.design: In-situ TEM deformation experiments to measure lattice distortion and dislocation mobility
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If lattice distortion is not correlated with dislocation mobility and mechanical properties, the hypothesis is falsified
